title: Nonvanishing of brackets in nonopposite root spaces
statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field and $L$ a finite-dimensional $K$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra] with nondegenerate Killing form $B(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(\operatorname{ad}(x)\operatorname{ad}(y))$. Let $H\subseteq L$ be a nilpotent self-normalizing subalgebra, meaning its lower central series eventually vanishes and $\{x\in L:[x,H]\subseteq H\}=H$, such that every $\operatorname{ad}(h)$ for $h\in H$ is diagonalizable over $K$. For $\gamma\in H^\vee$ write $L_\gamma=\{x\in L:[h,x]=\gamma(h)x\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Let $\alpha,\beta\in H^\vee$ be nonzero, with $\alpha+\beta\ne0$ and $L_\alpha,L_\beta,L_{\alpha+\beta}$ all nonzero. For every nonzero $x\in L_\alpha$ and $y\in L_\beta$ one has $[x,y]\ne0$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed p.503 (split characteristic-zero root-space theory assumed there) and Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509 (nonzero bracket constants). This general-field local statement is agent-formulated; the root-string proof for an arbitrary split form, without assuming an already chosen Chevalley basis, needs Serre, Complex Semisimple Lie Algebras, Chapters V--VI, WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-killing-cartan-rank-one-spaces]. Its triangularizability hypothesis follows from the assumed diagonalizability. Its generalized spaces equal the ordinary $L_\gamma$: ordinary eigenvectors are generalized eigenvectors, and the cited statement gives the converse. Thus $L_\alpha$ and $L_\beta$ are one-dimensional. Obtain $c\in H$, $u\in L_\alpha$, $v\in L_{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha(c)=2$, $[u,v]=c$, $[c,u]=2u$, $[c,v]=-2v$. Write $x=au$ with $a\in K^\times$ and set $f=a^{-1}v$. Then $(c,x,f)$ is an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ triple: $[x,f]=c$, $[c,x]=2x$, $[c,f]=-2f$, and $c\ne0$ since $\alpha(c)=2$. Put $E=\operatorname{ad}(x)$ and $F=\operatorname{ad}(f)$.

proof.text: Jacobi gives $[t,[x,w]]=[[t,x],w]+[x,[t,w]]=(\alpha(t)+\gamma(t))[x,w]$ for $w\in L_\gamma$ and $t\in H$. Hence $E(L_\gamma)\subseteq L_{\gamma+\alpha}$ and likewise $F(L_\gamma)\subseteq L_{\gamma-\alpha}$. By [lem-sfb-nilpotent-module-generalized-weight-decomposition] only finitely many generalized weights of the adjoint $H$-module $L$ occur; every nonzero ordinary weight space is among them. The functions $\gamma+j\alpha$ for $j\ge0$ are distinct: evaluate at any $t$ with $\alpha(t)\ne0$ and use characteristic zero. Therefore for any $z\in L_\gamma$, some $E^jz$ is zero. This proves precisely the termination needed below.

proof.text: Suppose for contradiction that $Ey=[x,y]=0$. In the finite-dimensional adjoint representation of $L$, the vector $y\ne0$ satisfies $[c,y]=\beta(c)y$. Apply [lem-sfb-sl2-primitive-lowering-string] to $(c,x,f)$ and $y$: there is $m\in\mathbf N$ with $\beta(c)=m\cdot1_K$.

proof.text: The lowering inclusion of step 2 places $F^{r+1}w$ in $L_\beta$. By the one-dimensionality of $L_\beta$ from [lem-sfb-killing-cartan-rank-one-spaces], write $F^{r+1}w=by$ for some $b\in K$. Then $EF^{r+1}w=bEy=0$, contradicting step 4. Thus $[x,y]\ne0$, for every pair of nonzero $x,y$ as asserted.
